title: Sell Mineral Rights in Conway, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Conway, AR | Faulkner County
metaDescription: Own gas royalty rights near Conway, Arkansas, the Faulkner County seat? We evaluate core Fayetteville Shale interests and make a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Conway is the Faulkner County seat and sits inside the structural core of the Fayetteville Shale, one of the most heavily drilled parts of the entire play.
intro: As Faulkner County's largest city and home to the University of Central Arkansas and Hendrix College, Conway has grown substantially in recent decades, and a fair amount of the land that once held mineral interests quietly has since been developed for housing and commercial use. The minerals underneath that land didn't go away with the development, they just became easier for owners to lose track of amid everything else happening on the surface.

sections.heading: Faulkner County at the heart of the Fayetteville Shale
paragraphs: Faulkner County was one of the most actively drilled counties during the Fayetteville Shale's 2005 to 2012 boom, and well density here was among the highest in the play. If your family held land in the county during that period, there's a good chance a lease was signed and, in many cases, a well was actually drilled and produced.

sections.heading: Urban growth and mineral ownership
paragraphs: As Conway has grown, some formerly rural tracts have been subdivided, developed, or sold multiple times, and the mineral estate doesn't always transfer as cleanly as the surface in those transactions. If your family's land near Conway has changed hands or been developed since the original lease was signed, it's worth confirming that you still hold the mineral rights before assuming you do.
We check the deed chain as part of any offer to make sure the interest we're evaluating is actually yours to sell.

sections.heading: Operator history: Southwestern Energy to BKV Corporation
paragraphs: Most original wells in this area were drilled by Southwestern Energy under its SEECO subsidiary. That position moved to Flywheel Energy in 2018 and then to BKV Corporation in 2021, so a name change on your royalty statement over the years reflects that history, not a problem with your interest.

faqs.question: Is Faulkner County part of the productive core of the Fayetteville Shale?
faqs.answer: Yes, it was one of the most heavily drilled counties in the play, with high well density during the 2005 to 2012 boom years.

faqs.question: Our land near Conway has been developed since the mineral rights were established. Do we still own them?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it depends on how the mineral estate was handled in subsequent sales. We check the deed chain to confirm.

faqs.question: Who operates the wells in this area today?
faqs.answer: Many legacy Fayetteville Shale wells in Faulkner County are now operated by BKV Corporation, following its 2021 acquisition of the position originally held by Southwestern Energy.
